# 201 — External_Connecting

Indicates that an explicit attempt to establish a connection to an external dependency is beginning\.

[All events](index.md) · [External category](Category_External.md) · [API reference](xref:Patware.Diagnostics.ApplicationEvents.ExternalEvents.Connecting%28System.String%2CSystem.String%2CSystem.String%29)

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| EventId | 201 |
| Name | External_Connecting |
| Category | [External](Category_External.md) |
| Event class | OperationalInformation |
| Log level | Information |
| Status | Stable |
| Introduced | 0.0.10 |

## Usage

Import `Patware.Diagnostics.ApplicationEvents`. This example assumes an existing
`ILogger` named `logger` and caller-supplied variables for the arguments.

```csharp
logger.External.Connecting(@externalName, @operationName, @operationId);
```

**Trigger:** Emit immediately before invoking an API whose purpose is to establish or acquire a connection\.

**Message template:** Connecting to external dependency \{ExternalName\}\. Operation: \{OperationName\}\. Attempt: \{OperationId\}\.

## Arguments

- `externalName` (`string`): The logical dependency name, without credentials or sensitive addresses\.
- `operationName` (`string`): The logical name of the explicit connection operation\.
- `operationId` (`string`): The identifier of this connection attempt, shared with its outcome\. Use a different identifier for each retry\.

## Remarks

- Define connection success according to the API being observed\. State whether it represents a transport connection, an authenticated session, or an acquired connection from a pool\.
- This event describes connection establishment, not an ordinary business operation performed through an existing connection\.
- Do not infer an explicit connection attempt merely because an HTTP request or other dependency operation is beginning\.
- Use the same external name, operation name, and operation identifier for the outcome of this attempt\.
- A successful connection attempt produces External\_Connected\. Authentication rejection, authorization denial, timeout, or unavailability may produce their corresponding failure events when established by the connection API\.
- The listed failure events are not an exhaustive classification of every possible connection error\. Do not relabel an unrelated exception as unavailability\.
- Cancellation, process termination, or an unclassified failure can prevent a corresponding catalog outcome\. Missing completion does not by itself prove unavailability\.
- Calling this method only emits a diagnostic record\. It does not establish connections, retry, or change application mode\.
